problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=y\,i+x\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $\operatorname{sin}⁡y=x-2$ traversed from the point $A(2,0)$ to the point $B(2,\pi ).$

activity_context.topic_title: Line Integrals of Vector-Valued Functions Over General Curves

examples.problem: Evaluate $\displaystyle \int\limits_{C} \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{r},$ where $\mathbf F(x, y) = y\,\mathbf{i} + x\,\mathbf{j}$ and $C$ is the curve $y^3 = x-5$ traversed from the point $A(5,0)$ to the point $B(6,1).$
examples.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int\limits_C \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{r} = \int_a^b \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t) \,\textrm{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making $x$ the subject of the equation, we have

$$
y^3 = x-5
\qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad
x = y^3 + 5.
$$

So, we can parametrize the curve using

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =({t}^{3}+5)\,i+t\,j,\,0\le t\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x = t^3+5, \qquad
y = t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =y\,i+x\,j \\  & =t\,i+({t}^{3}+5)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $\mathbf{r}'(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}+5)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(t\,i+({t}^{3}+5)\,j)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j) \\  & =t\cdot 3{t}^{2}+({t}^{3}+5)\cdot 1 \\  & =3{t}^{3}+{t}^{3}+5 \\  & =4{t}^{3}+5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{t}^{3}+5\,dt \\  & ={[{t}^{4}+5t]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =1+5-0 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=\frac{1}{x+y}\,i+\frac{2y}{x+y}\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(0,1)$ to the point $B(3,0).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=j$ and $b=3\,i.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(j)+t(3\,i-j) \\  & =3t\,i+(1-t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3t\,y=1-t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\frac{1}{x+y}\,i+\frac{2y}{x+y}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{3t+1-t}\,i+\frac{2-2t}{3t+1-t}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2t+1}\,i+\frac{2-2t}{2t+1}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-t)j \\  & =3\,i-j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\frac{1}{2t+1}\,i+\frac{2-2t}{2t+1}\,j)\cdot (3\,i-j) \\  & =\frac{1}{2t+1}\cdot 3+\frac{2-2t}{2t+1}\cdot (-1) \\  & =\frac{3-2+2t}{2t+1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}1\,dt \\  & =t{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =1-0 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$
